arxiv-2103-14564.title: From anyons to Majoranas
arxiv-2103-14564.creator: Jay Sau, 1,2,3 Steven Simon, 4 Smitha Vishveshwara, 5 James R. Williams 1,2,6∗ 1 Department of Physics, University of Maryland, College Park, MD, USA 2 Joint Quantum Institute, University of Maryland, College Park, MD, USA 3 Condensed Matter Theory Center, University of Maryland, College Park, MD, U
arxiv-2103-14564.description: Abstract Anyons, particles that are neither bosons nor fermions, were predicted in the 1980s, but strong experimental evidence for the existence of the simplest type on anyons has only emerged this year. Further theoretical and experimental advances promise to nail the existence of more exotic types on anyons, such as Majorana fermions, which would make topological quantum computation possible.

arxiv-2210-07857.title: Commutativity and Disentanglement from the Manifold Perspective
arxiv-2210-07857.creator: Frank Qiu frankqiu@berkeley.edu
arxiv-2210-07857.description: Abstract In this paper, we interpret disentanglement as the discovery of local charts of the data manifold and trace how this definition naturally leads to an equivalent condition for disentanglement: commutativity between factors of variation. We study the impact of this manifold framework to two classes of problems: learning matrix exponential operators and compressing data-generating models.

arxiv-2304-11830.title: Chern-Simons Theory, Ehrhart Polynomials, and Representation Theory arXiv: 2304.11830
arxiv-2304-11830.creator: Chao Ju
arxiv-2304-11830.description: Abstract The Hilbert space of level q q Chern-Simons theory of gauge group G G of the ADE type quantized on T 2 T^{2} can be represented by points that lie on the weight lattice of the Lie algebra 𝔤 \mathfrak{g} up to some discrete identifications. Of special significance are the points that also lie on the root lattice.

arxiv-2305-14825.title: Large Language Models are In-Context Semantic Reasoners rather than Symbolic Reasoners
arxiv-2305-14825.creator: Xiaojuan Tang, Zilong Zheng, Jiaqi Li, Fanxu Meng, Song-Chun Zhu, Yitao Liang, Muhan Zhang
arxiv-2305-14825.description: Abstract The emergent few-shot reasoning capabilities of Large Language Models (LLMs) have excited the natural language and machine learning community over recent years. Despite of numerous successful applications, the underlying mechanism of such in-context capabilities still remains unclear. In this work, we hypothesize that the learned semantics of language tokens do the most heavy lifting during the reasoning process.

arxiv-2405-09749.title: Low-frequency, wideband study of an active repeater, FRB 20240114A, with the GMRT
arxiv-2405-09749.creator: U. Panda, J. Roy, S. Bhattacharyya, C. Dudeja, S. Kudale
arxiv-2405-09749.description: Abstract We report the detection of a total of 135 bursts from a recently discovered active, repeating fast radio burst, FRB 20240114A with the GMRT over a frequency range of 300 − - 750 MHz. The bursts were detected with intrinsic widths ranging from 0.308 to 39.364 ms, a median scattering timescale of 2.059 ms at 400 MHz and 1.

arxiv-2405-13632.title: Task agnostic continual learning with Pairwise layer architecture
arxiv-2405-13632.creator: Santtu Keskinen
arxiv-2405-13632.description: Abstract Most of the dominant approaches to continual learning are based on either memory replay, parameter isolation, or regularization techniques that require task boundaries to calculate task statistics. We propose a static architecture-based method that doesn’t use any of these.

arxiv-2409-01042.title: Annealing-inspired training of an optical neural network with ternary weights
arxiv-2409-01042.creator: Anas Skalli, Mirko Goldmann, Nasibeh Haghighi, Stephan Reitzenstein, James A. Lott, Daniel Brunner
arxiv-2409-01042.description: Abstract Artificial neural networks (ANNs) represent a fundamentally connectionnist and distributed approach to computing, and as such they differ from classical computers that utilize the von Neumann architecture. This has revived research interest in new unconventional hardware to enable more efficient implementations of ANNs rather than emulating them on traditional machines.

arxiv-2409-15537.title: Quasi-Monte Carlo integration for feedback control under uncertainty
arxiv-2409-15537.creator: Philipp A. Guth, Peter Kritzer, Karl Kunisch
arxiv-2409-15537.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Philipp A. Guth, Peter Kritzer, Karl Kunisch. A control in feedback form is derived for linear quadratic, time-invariant optimal control problems subject to parabolic partial differential equations with coefficients depending on a countably infinite number of uncertain parameters. It is shown that the Riccati-based feedback operator depends analytically on the parameters provided that the system operator depends analytically on the parameters, as is the case, for instance, in diffusion problems when the diffusion coefficient is parameterized by a Karhunen–Loève expansion.

pmc-11499652.title: LncRNA MSTRG.13,871/miR155-5p/Grip1 network involved in the post-cardiac arrest brain injury
pmc-11499652.creator: Yiwei Li, Chenghao Wu, Xin Wen, Wei Hu, Mengyuan Diao
pmc-11499652.description: Post-cardiac arrest brain (PCABI) is a severe medical condition characterized by a significant risk of neurological impairment and death. Nevertheless, the specific process and essential molecules responsible for its development are not fully understood. Profiling based on competing endogenous RNAs (ceRNA) has been implicated in the onset and progression of neurological disorders, yet its role in PCABI remains unclear.

pmc-12733449.title: Pheromone Race Composition of Ostrinia nubilalis (Lepidoptera: Crambidae) and Larval Co-Occurrence with Sesamia nonagrioides (Lepidoptera: Noctuidae) in Maize in Central-Eastern Italy
pmc-12733449.creator: Maria Chiara Battistelli, Diego Palpacelli, Giorgio Sperandio, Matteo Pacella, Fabio Ramilli, Sara Ruschioni, Abdalhadi M. A. Abulebda, Paola Riolo
pmc-12733449.description: Simple SummaryOstrinia nubilalis and Sesamia nonagrioides are important maize pests in central-eastern Mediterranean Europe, with larvae boring into plants, causing yield losses. This study investigated the corn borer species present in central-eastern Italy, the presence and prevalence of O. nubilalis pheromone races, and the within-plant larval distribution across three plant sections (lower and upper stalk and ear).

pmc-12887209.creator: Nikolaos Stalikas, Takuya Mizukami, Frederic Bouisset, Kazumasa Ikeda, Atomu Tajima, Daniel Munhoz, Thabo Mahendiran, Adriaan Wilgenhof, Koshiro Sakai, Bjarne Noorgard, Thomas Engstroem, Jonathon Leipsic, Giulio Stefanini, Antonio Bartorelli, Timothy Fairbairn, Alan Bagnall, Brian Ko, Nils P Johnson
pmc-12887209.description: BackgroundAssessing the myocardial mass at risk is essential in evaluating patients with coronary artery disease. This study aims to establish reference values for vessel‐specific myocardial mass derived from coronary computed tomography angiography, providing a quantitative assessment of the myocardial mass subtended by each epicardial vessel.

pmc-13538577.title: Mineralogical and geochemical provenance reference for turquoise from the Teghout Cu–Mo deposit in Armenia
pmc-13538577.creator: Bahareh Shirdam, Mingxing Yang, Khachatur Meliksetian, Edmond Grigoryan, Yue Yang, Yuwei Zheng, Xin Wan, Yan Jiang
pmc-13538577.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Turquoise from the Teghout Cu–Mo porphyry deposit (Lori Province, northern Armenia) forms veinlets and nodules in the supergene zone with quartz, Fe–Mn oxides, jarosite, barite and clay minerals, locally chalcanthite and gypsum. We provide the first integrated reference dataset for a substantial Caucasus turquoise source, providing the mineralogical and geochemical reference data needed to support future archaeological provenance research, collection authentication and heritage-science studies of exchange in the region.

pmc-13730441.title: Cu-Catalyzed Reductive Coupling of Allylic and Carbonyl Electrophiles
pmc-13730441.creator: Vaughn Beale, Ming Chen
pmc-13730441.description: We report herein Cu-catalyzed syntheses of secondary and tertiary homoallylic alcohols. Compared to conventional carbonyl addition with nucleophilic allylation reagents, this process utilizes a reductive coupling strategy in which electrophilic allylic esters couple with carbonyl compounds with B2pin2 as the reductant. Notably, the approach employs an earth-abundant metal catalyst without using cryogenic conditions.
